answer: Sybil resistance here rests on proof-of-work bound to the epoch and to the claiming wallet: you burn compute on a hash target, and each address owns its nonce chain, so a proof cannot be replayed by a copycat account. Reputation also sits behind collateral, a jetty of bond backing each identity and slashed on collusion, so a canyon of sock puppets is costly. Rewards split by real work, so slicing one stake into many heads earns nothing extra while charging every head its bond, hash grind, and fees. Reaching the summit of a tier therefore costs an attacker the full stake a thousand times.
